# Start where the thread is loose

"There may be a story in this transcript. Map the money, roles, resources and decision rights behind it. Show me the most useful geometry, then follow the strongest lead."

"I suspect these groups have a common patron. Treat that as my working prior. Look for the mechanism that would distinguish patron direction from independent agreement."

"Take this existing case and show me what was connected before the policy announcement. Keep unknown dates visible."

"This investigation has become a hairball. Build the atlas, start with the major workstreams, and let me inspect the evidence behind the cross-group bridges."

"That original report was corrected. Show which findings depend on it or its copies, then revisit the affected explanations."

"Who can credibly withhold something the other actors need? Compare their moves, outside options and likely responses, with the assumptions visible."

"Turn the strongest supported mechanism into a sharp article. Challenge the key claims first and preserve the missing records that still matter."

## Try the fictional case

Render `examples/meridian-case.json` into an explicitly chosen new output path using the render command in the case-format reference. Open the resulting HTML in a modern browser. Explore the foundation/institute relationship, inspect the copied-report ancestry, compare the hypotheses, and inspect the dates on the adviser's roles. Treat every name and source in this fixture as fictional.

The worthwhile question is what evidence would separate funding, compatible beliefs, shared advisers and actual approval rights. The map makes those differences inspectable; it does not decide motives from proximity.
